On quant soundness, B's S3 tests each feature two ways, by rank-IC and by a per-window gradient-boosted drop-column ML information-gain test (SIG-05, SIGML family, `ml_gain` step). That meets the brief's 'test them with ML for information gain'. A tests only rank correlation. B also benchmarks S4 against the best of the classical portfolios, which matches 'must beat the stage-2 classical portfolios'. A benchmarks against minimum variance alone. B's roadmap gives every milestone checkable Exit criteria and assigns RF-01 to M4 and RF-02/RF-03 to M6/M7. A has Exit criteria only on M1 and lists no References on any later milestone. In the M1 plan, B fixes real buildability and graph defects that A still has. In A, M1-T05 must 'append as parts' while `store/parts.py` belongs to the parallel M1-T06, and the T05 packet lacks AD-06. B moves parts.py to T05, adds AD-06, and records the real T06→T05 code edge. In A, M1-T39 must honour overrides but `check_moves` only takes a ReturnsPanel and no task writes `overrides.py`; B adds the Snapshot input and the overrides module. A's `open_run` signatures in PL-09 and PL-10 disagree; B unifies them. A labels M1-T48 as package app although it writes a server file and gates on app. B also moves the resume test TC-22 into the system task and adds the stopped-run heartbeat check to T02. Both sets still share some issues: stale '(new)' markers on files that earlier tasks created, and a large interface task.
